author: Thordur Arnason
title: Clairic: extraction at $0.10 per million input tokens
summary: Cloudflare’s extraction preview charges for input only. The practical test is cost per accepted extraction, including validation and human review.
paragraphs: An invoice number, a delivery date or a receipt total is a small job to give a general-purpose language model. Cloudflare’s Clairic offers a specialist alternative: define the fields you need and receive typed values, with confidence scores for extracted answers and intervals for estimates.

Released on 19 October as a Workers AI preview, Clairic is available through the @cf/cloudflare/clairic endpoint. The posted rate is $0.10 per million input tokens, with no output-token charge. It accepts text and up to four images. Check the API’s reported usage when budgeting: field definitions contribute tokens, and requests can span multiple processing passes.

The economics are promising for repetitive document work, but a correctly formatted answer can still be wrong. Cloudflare describes limitations in multi-step arithmetic and forecasting, and says uncertainty intervals can be too narrow on unfamiliar data. Extract the facts, use code for calculations and test review thresholds on representative documents. Cloudflare’s performance claims still need validation on your workload.
Open weights are planned; the announcement makes the hosted preview available now. Treat self-hosting as a future option until downloadable weights and license terms are available.

The useful comparison is cost per accepted extraction. Count the model call, retries, validation and human review against your current pipeline. A lower token bill matters most when it also reduces the cost of getting a correct result.

author: Thordur Arnason
title: Mercury 3: launch prices and the Mercury 2 migration deadline
summary: Mercury 3 launches at half its regular token rates. Existing direct customers of Mercury 2 and 2.5 have until 15 November to migrate, with enterprise agreements treated separately.
paragraphs: Mercury 3 launched on 19 October at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.35 per million output tokens, half its regular $0.20/$0.70 rates. Cached input costs $0.01 per million tokens during the offer. No promotion end date is stated on the checked pricing pages.

Inception has also closed Mercury 2 and 2.5 to new direct customers. Customers with usage before 19 October retain access until 15 November; enterprise agreements are treated separately. That is Inception’s policy, not a confirmed shutdown of every third-party route.
Budget against both tariffs and test migration before the deadline.
calculatorGuidance: Compare Mercury 3’s current routed Tape quote with Haiku 5.5’s Standard plan using your workload. For a regular-rate Mercury scenario, enter $0.20 input and $0.70 output per million tokens under Your rate overrides. Check your host’s cache terms separately; the launch offer has no stated end date.

author: Thordur Arnason
title: AI model releases: 12–16 October 2026
summary: Gemini 4 Argon and Muse Wonder expand the API choices. Muse Spark Open and NVIDIA’s Nemotron releases bring new deployment options. A review of the week so far, with access and costs checked.
paragraphs: This week’s releases widen the choice of both rented and self-hosted intelligence. The useful distinction is what you can access today: a production API, a preview, downloadable weights or a subscription. Those differences belong beside the price.

releases.name: Muse Wonder / Wonder Full
releases.terms: Wonder: $4 / $20. Wonder Full requires a Muse Code Power or Maximum subscription.
releases.implication: The API price buys Wonder. Full is a separate access decision.

releases.name: Gemini 4 Argon
releases.terms: Standard: $2 / $10 until 30 November; $4 / $20 from 1 December. Implicit caching only.
releases.implication: Price a continuing workload at both rates before migrating.

releases.name: Ultramarine 1 Flash
releases.terms: $0.15 / $0.50 on the publisher’s API. The model page still says weights are coming soon.
releases.implication: A GLM-5.3 Flash post-train for professional work. Test its claimed savings on your own tasks.

releases.name: Grok Voice 3.0
releases.terms: $0.08 per minute, unchanged from Voice 2.0. The grok-voice-latest alias has switched over.
releases.implication: Retest existing voice agents. Per-minute billing needs a different comparison from text tokens.

releases.name: Muse Spark Open
releases.terms: Custom Muse Model License. Meta supplies BF16 and NVFP4 checkpoints.
releases.implication: Budget hardware and check license conditions before treating downloadable weights as a saving.

releases.name: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL
releases.implication: Adds an option for multimodal agents; active parameters alone do not size a deployment.

releases.name: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B
releases.terms: Targets a 24 GB model footprint through compression and mixed-precision quantization.
releases.implication: Allow additional memory for context and runtime. Published laptop measurements used 128 GB systems.

takeaways.title: Compare the bill you will actually pay.
takeaways.text: Argon’s introductory rate has an end date. Wonder Full is sold by subscription. Opus Fast changes the service rate. A single headline price cannot represent all three decisions.

takeaways.title: Put open weights through a capacity calculation.
takeaways.text: Spark Open, Super VL and Bolt occupy different hardware budgets. Measure memory, throughput, utilization and operational effort before choosing ownership over a hosted route.

takeaways.title: Measure the cost of completed work.
takeaways.text: Use representative tasks and count retries and human review. Publisher benchmarks are useful leads; they do not establish quality or cost parity on your workload.

updates.title: Opus 5.5 Fast · 15 October
updates.text: Fast mode left research preview at $8 / $40 per million tokens. It serves the same model at a premium rate; it is not a new Opus release.

watching.title: MAI-Base-2 · 15 October
watching.text: Microsoft completed pre-training; post-training continues. Partner weight licensing through Foundry is planned. This announcement does not establish a public API or downloadable release.

watching.title: GLM-Legal · 13 October
watching.text: Z.ai opened applications for API beta access. The post says AutoClaw integration is forthcoming; no public token tariff is stated there.

watching.title: Bolt E4B · expected 23 October
watching.text: NVIDIA’s smaller Bolt variant is scheduled for next week. Availability still needs checking on release day.

coverage: A selected review of releases relevant to buying and running AI, checked through Friday morning. Weekend releases are outside this pilot’s cutoff. Step 5 Preview’s weights were verified by this site this week; that observation alone does not date their release. Prices and availability can change after this edition.

author: Thordur Arnason
title: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL and Bolt: model size and local deployment
summary: NVIDIA’s Bolt compresses Super VL for local deployment. A smaller model footprint changes the hardware calculation; it does not settle the bill.
paragraphs: NVIDIA’s Super VL and Bolt arrived on 15 October with different deployment requirements. Super VL carries 120 billion parameters; Bolt compresses that architecture to 74 billion, then uses mixed-precision quantization to target a 24 GB model footprint.
The machine also needs memory for context, runtime and other applications. NVIDIA’s published laptop measurements used a 128 GB system.

Super VL already has hosted API quotes. Bolt makes local ownership another option to measure. Compare hardware, power, utilization and successful-task costs when estimating the cost of running locally.
calculatorTitle: What does running it yourself cost?
calculatorGuidance: Rent vs Run opens Super VL’s hosted quote in custom deployment mode. Enter your measured memory, throughput and operating costs. Bolt is a different model with no hosted tariff verified here; its 24 GB footprint is not a Super VL preset, and quality equivalence is not assumed.

author: Thordur Arnason
title: Muse Spark Open: deployment hardware and license terms
summary: Muse Spark Open’s weights are available under custom terms. Compare its deployment hardware and licensing conditions with hosted API prices.
paragraphs: Meta released Muse Spark Open on 15 October; downloading its checkpoints requires approval. Its NVFP4 deployment example uses four Blackwell Ultra GPUs or eight H200s.

Under the license, model-as-a-service businesses above $20 million in aggregate revenue, including affiliates, need a separate agreement. Internal use and products outside that category have exemptions.

The hosted quote checked on 16 October is $1.25 input and $4.25 output per million tokens. Compare that bill with the hardware, utilization and operating costs of running it yourself. Downloadable weights still leave someone paying for the machines.

author: Thordur Arnason
title: Step 5 Preview: weights, hardware and license terms
summary: Step 5 Preview’s weights are public. Its active parameter count tells only part of the deployment story.
paragraphs: Step 5 Preview’s weights are now downloadable. It activates 27 billion parameters per token, but carries roughly 600 billion in total. StepFun’s FP8 deployment examples use four B300 GPUs or eight H200s.

Its custom license also includes attribution and commercial-license conditions. Before comparing API bills with self-hosting, count the hardware, runtime and licensing requirements. author: Thordur Arnason
title: Gemini 4 Argon: API prices double on 1 December
summary: Gemini 4 Argon’s posted token prices double on 1 December. Budget recurring work using both the introductory and scheduled rates.
paragraphs: Gemini 4 Argon arrived on 13 October with introductory pricing: $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens. Google’s published standard rates double to $4 and $20 on 1 December.
Budget recurring work at both prices, include thinking tokens in output, and check the cache assumptions: Argon supports implicit caching only.
calculatorTitle: Price your workload at both Argon rates
calculatorGuidance: Compare Argon with GPT-6.1 Sol using your input, output and thinking volumes. Select Standard through 2026-11-30 or Standard from 2026-12-01 to examine the scheduled increase. Implicit cache hits are an assumption; explicit cache writes are unsupported. The calculator uses Argon’s default synchronous output limit.

author: Thordur Arnason
title: Muse Wonder: API pricing and Wonder Full access
summary: Muse Wonder’s API rates match Opus 5.5. Wonder Full is available through specific Muse Code subscriptions.
paragraphs: Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full have different access and billing arrangements.

Muse Wonder launched on 12 October in preview. Its API costs $4 input and $20 output per million tokens, matching Claude Opus 5.5’s standard token prices. Meta’s provider ID is muse-wonder-1.0; OpenRouter routes it as meta/muse-wonder.

Muse Wonder Full is a separate model available only through Muse Code’s Power Usage or Maximum Usage subscriptions. Raising the API’s reasoning effort does not select Full. Keep Full’s results separate when comparing the model your API bill buys.
calculatorGuidance: Compare Muse Wonder’s OpenRouter tape quote with Opus 5.5’s published Standard plan using your actual input and output volumes. Muse Code subscription costs are outside this token comparison.

author: Thordur Arnason
title: Haiku 5.5: higher API rates above 100,000 prompt tokens
summary: The 100,000-token boundary changes both input and output rates. Price agent workloads by prompt length, with cached tokens included.
paragraphs: Haiku 5.5’s standard API rate starts at $0.10 input and $0.50 output per million tokens for prompts up to 100,000 tokens. Above that threshold, the rates rise to $0.50 input and $2.50 output.

Anthropic counts cached reads and cache writes toward a request’s prompt length. Each request is priced individually, so a cache hit can reduce billable cost while the prompt still crosses into the higher tariff.
For long conversations and agent runs, context management changes the tariff as well as the number of billable tokens. A one-million-token context window comes with more than one price band.
calculatorGuidance: Compare with Haiku 4.5 using your actual prompt sizes, cache use and output volumes. Choose Standard or Standard long context for Haiku 5.5 to match your prompt length before estimating savings.
